Innovation for the Earth




Integrated Report 2026
Year Ended March 31, 2026
Innovation for the Earth
To realize a sustainable society, we support the basis of LIFE and
will continue to create peace of mind for generations to come.
Viewing changes in the social environment as a business opportunity, SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group is working to
continuously generate innovation to help resolve social issues drawing on the solutions created by its varied and diverse
technologies as well as the trust it enjoys with its stakeholders.
By contributing to the Earth and people’s lives, we are endeavoring to enhance the sustainability of society in concert with
efforts to secure our sustainable growth as a company.

Message from the President & CEO


                                                                                                                                                 Turning challenges
                                                                                                                                                 into results
                                                                                                                                                 with Accelerate 2028
                                                                                                                                                 to realize Vision 2030

                                                                                                                                                            At the Midpoint of Vision 2030
                                                                                                                                                         Toward the Launch of Accelerate 2028

                                                                                                                                                 In 2020, the SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group announced Vision
                                                                                                                                                 2030, which aims to double the scale of our business by
                                                                                                                                                 FY2030. Today, all Group employees are working as one
                                                                                                                                                 toward its realization. Under former President Kato, we drove
                                                                                                                                                 growth over the five years from 2020 and firmly established
                                                                                                                                                 momentum, including by achieving record-high profits. The
                                                                                                                                                 year 2026 marks both the exact midpoint of Vision 2030 and
                                                                                                                                                 the important milestone of launching a new Medium-term
                                                                                                                                                 Management Plan. Having assumed responsibility for steering
                                                                                                                                                 management at this juncture, I feel the weight of that
                                                                                                                                                 responsibility keenly. As its name suggests, the new
                                                                                                                                                 Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 is a
                                                                                                                                                 three-year period for accelerating growth toward the


                                                                                     TOP Message
                                                                                                                                                 realization of Vision 2030. I believe my role, having received
    President & CEO                                                                                                                              the baton, is to ensure that we execute this plan.
                                                                                                                                                     Through Accelerate 2028, we will turn challenges into
                                                                                                                                                 tangible results and make a concerted effort to realize
I joined SEKISUI CHEMICAL in 1987 and began my career as an engineer working on adhesive tape for corrugated                                     Innovation for the Earth, the vision statement set forth in our
cardboard packaging. Since then, I have pursued my career in the High Performance Plastics Company. A major turning                              Long-term Vision, Vision 2030.
point came in 2006, when I was assigned to the United States. As president of a local subsidiary whose performance was
struggling at the time, I faced the difficult decision of whether to rebuild the business or withdraw from it. Working
together with employees to implement reforms aimed at rebuilding the business, we achieved record-high profit for the
first time in 10 years, which gave me tremendous confidence. After returning to Japan, I served as head of the Interlayer
Film and Foam Division, and from 2019, as President of the High Performance Plastics Company, I was also involved in the
acquisition and PMI of SEKISUI AEROSPACE CORPORATION. I believe the valuable experience I gained through business
revitalization, acquisitions, and integration will be of great use in management going forward.                                                                              SEKISUI CHEMICAL Integrated Report 2026   02

SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group’s Business Domains
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group is active in the Residential and Social Infrastructure Creation and Chemical Solutions business. We have developed business in the four domains of “Residential,” “Advanced Lifeline,”
“Innovative Mobility,” and “Life Science.” We produce a large number of Products to Enhance Sustainability by making a high degree of contribution to solving natural and social environmental issues, as a result, these
products have consistently accounted for more than 70% of total company sales.
The current business consists of four segments and the three divisional companies of Housing, Urban Infrastructure & Environmental Products (UIEP), and High Performance Plastics (HPP), as well as the Medical Business.

Value Creation Process
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group provides Products to Enhance Sustainability, which are products and services that help improve people’s lives and the global environment, strategically addressing social issues based on
relationships of trust with stakeholders and myriad technologies. By effectively utilizing the six forms of capital and implementing our business models, we will create Products to Enhance Sustainability and convert
their impact into competitiveness, as well as increase our six forms of capital to improve the sustainability of society and achieve sustainable growth as a company.
    We will continue to take on the challenge of realizing a sustainable society by delivering to society “peace of mind for generations to come,” which means that “peace of mind for living will continue not only for us
living now, but also for the next generation and into the future.”

 Commentary               Value Creation Process

Value co-creation with stakeholders through business models
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group’s strengths are Strategic Foresight, Processing and Value Transformation.
  Through collaboration with varied and diverse stakeholders, the Company practices a business model centered on these three strengths in a way that creates products and services that help solve issues facing the natural and
social environments.
  Through this cycle, we will create positive impacts on the environment and society, convert this into competitiveness, increase both financial and non-financial capital, and strive to sustainably increase corporate value.

Risks and Opportunities
General Risks
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group believes that it is important to appropriately control enterprise risks from short-term and medium- to long-term perspectives, seize opportunities, and establish an environment conducive to taking on risk
for growth.
   Rather than viewing matters that could significantly affect investment decisions solely as risks, we also recognize their potential as opportunities and address them strategically from both perspectives.
   Based on this recognition, the Group identifies the possibility of occurrence of various risks and opportunities, and seek to establish and operate systems that enable prompt and appropriate responses.
   For the general risks listed below, response measures are discussed and decisions are made through the Board of Directors, Sustainability Committee, quarterly budget meetings, the relevant area-specific committees, the Risk
Review committee, and other bodies.

Risks and Opportunities
Megatrends
In addition to general risks, we take into account irreversible changes in the external environment that could affect the Group’s business (hereinafter referred to as megatrends). Based on various scenarios, we assess their frequency
and impact on management from a medium- to long-term perspective, and newly organize and identify material risks and opportunities for the Group.
   We currently consider the following 12 megatrends to be important for the Group, and have reflected them in the strategies of our Medium-term Management Plan. Going forward, we plan to further build and operate
mechanisms to review these trends while identifying and tracking environmental changes.

Risks and Opportunities
Risks and Opportunities Based on TCFD Scenario Analysis (Megatrend: Climate Change)
Recognizing that climate change will have a significant impact on management in the short to long term, and will present risks and opportunities for our businesses, we have formulated an Environmental Medium-term Plan by
backcasting from 2050. See P.43
  To identify these risks and opportunities, we envisage four social scenarios based on two axes: the extent of progress toward a carbon-neutral society and the extent of progress toward a circular economy. We verify the validity of
our strategies under each scenario, set milestones toward realizing both a carbon-neutral society and a circular economy, and formulate strategies to accelerate our initiatives. For details, please see our TCFD/TNFD Report

Key Issues (Materiality)
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group has identified eight key issues (materiality) to address as priorities in pursuit of sustainable growth, and is advancing initiatives accordingly.
   Among these key issues, initiatives in areas positioned as Value Creation Fields help capture growth opportunities through the creation and expansion of Products to Enhance Sustainability. In particular, we believe
that creating highly profitable Premium Framework products will contribute to improving ROIC over the medium to long term. Meanwhile, initiatives related to materiality positioned as Value Creation Drivers help
curb increases in the broader cost of capital* by strengthening the business foundation and reducing risk.
   In other words, addressing materiality contributes to expanding the Sekisui Sustainable Spread—the difference between ROIC and the broader cost of capital—and, as a result, enhances corporate value over the
medium to long term.
* Broader cost of capital: An expanded concept of the cost of capital used in a conventional ROIC spread that newly incorporates non-financial KPIs capable of affecting long-term corporate value.

Products to Enhance Sustainability

About the Premium Framework
The Premium Framework is a strategic framework that combines solutions to issues in the natural and social environments with profitability.
   The Premium Framework certifies products that drive the growth of each divisional company, and approximately 70% of Premium Framework net sales are generated by products from businesses categorized as growth-driving
or growth-potential businesses.
   We will accelerate the expansion of the Premium Framework by aggressively allocating capital to these two categories.

Products to Enhance Sustainability

Promoting the Environmental Value of Products
In response to, or ahead of, the demands of society and customers, SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group is promoting the value of low-carbon and decarbonized products that contribute to mitigating climate change issues. In order to convey
to customers the value of low-carbon and decarbonized products, we calculate the carbon footprint of our products based on carbon life cycle assessments (C-LCA). Calculations are made by setting parameters according to each
objective and product. For raw materials, at present, calculations are based on a database (IDEA) with publicly available average GHG emission coefficients. We believe that as progress is made with initiatives at raw material
manufacturers and coordination with the supply chain, we will be able to leverage the low-carbon value of each company’s efforts. The amount of raw materials used, energy used in production, and other data are calculated using
actual measurement data from production plants.

Long-term Vision, Vision 2030

Medium- to Long-term Strategies for Growth — Strategic Area Map —
We have revised the strategic area map to act as a compass for business strategies so we can realize our Long-term Vision, Vision 2030. Areas that are extensions of existing businesses and will be expanded on a
priority basis are called Enhancement Areas, while areas that will create new innovations through fusion of different areas are called Innovation Areas. We have established the four domains of Residential, Advanced
Lifeline, Innovative Mobility, and Life Science, along with Next Frontier as a new domain. By clarifying the themes to be targeted in each domain, we are prioritizing allocation of capital to focus on expanding the
Enhancement Areas and creating new innovations in the Innovation Areas.
   In particular, for the themes in the Innovation Areas, we are working not only with internal resources, but also with external resources through M&A and Corporate Venture Capital (CVC).

Materiality and KPIs
At the halfway point of our Long-term Vision, Vision 2030, we reanalyzed global megatrends, including climate change and advances in AI technology, and redefined the priority issues that we need to address.
   We are carrying out risk mitigation activities and, under the Medium-term Management Plan, we have defined the five areas of “Safety, Quality, Legal/Ethical, Accounting, and Information Management” in order
to avoid damage to corporate value from major incidents, and to enhance our management ability to sustain business.

Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 (FY2026-2028)

Returns to Shareholders
Under the Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028, SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group will return profits to its shareholders more aggressively than ever before. The Company will raise the dividend-on-equity
(DOE) ratio to 3.5% or higher, while continuously targeting a payout ratio of 40% or higher on a consolidated basis, and implement stable returns through progressive dividends. In addition, SEKISUI CHEMICAL
Group has set a target of 50% or higher for its total return ratio, which includes the buyback of shares, so long as its net D/E ratio is 0.5 or less. For this reason, the Company will also implement additional returns as
appropriate, taking into account the investment progress under the Medium-term Management Plan, cash position, and stock price. We will limit our holdings of treasury shares to the absolute minimum.

 Business Strategies               Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-driving Businesses: Device Materials, Specialty Chemicals, and FC (Electronics)
With the upswing in global semiconductor demand accompanying the proliferation of AI, the Electronics field is also performing well, especially for semiconductor-related products.
  In particular, we are seeing a steady increase in the application of SELFA, a UV release tape for semiconductor applications that addresses the further miniaturization of semiconductors, and Build-up dielectric film (BUF) that
boasts high transmission performance (low dielectric properties)—required for multi-layered CPUs—as well as strengths in suppressing substrate warpage.

 Business Strategies                             Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-driving and Growth-potential Businesses:
                                                 Interlayer Films and Automotive Molding/Aeronautical Components (Mobility), and Sensing/Molding Products (Industrial)
There are clear indications of a growth trajectory in the context of the expansion of the electrification of automobiles and automated driving.
  In our mainstay interlayer film business, we are working to improve profitability by shifting to high-value-added products such as wedge-shape films for head-up displays (HUDs), heat insulation films and colored/designed films,
while further increasing added value by combining interlayer film functions such as heat and sound insulation.
  In the aeronautical fields as well, we will steadily capture robust demand for commercial aircraft while expanding in the rapidly growing air mobility field, including drones.

Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 (FY2026-2028)

 Business Strategies               Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-potential Businesses: Housing, Renovation, Residential, and Overseas
In the Housing Business, we will pursue sales strategies suited to urban and regional areas based on market conditions and regional characteristics, aiming to increase both volume and profitability.
   In the Renovation Business, we will pursue further growth by expanding orders for older homes, which are expected to increase going forward, strengthening organizational structures in areas with demand, and utilizing M&A.
   In the Residential Business, we will strengthen the earnings base by increasing the number of rental properties under management while targeting significant growth in the purchase-and-resale business.
   Through proactive investment in the growth areas of Renovation and Residential, we will move away from a portfolio overly weighted toward the Housing Business.

Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 (FY2026-2028)

 Business Strategies                Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-potential Businesses: Performance Materials and Fire Resistant and Non-flammable Materials
                                    (Building and Infrastructures Composite Material), and Pipe Renewal (Infrastructure Renovation)
The Company aims to achieve growth by expanding sales of prioritized products that help solve labor shortages, infrastructure aging, climate change, and other social issues, as well as by increasing overseas net sales.
  As an example, FFU for railway sleepers, a mainstay product of the Performance Materials Business, are sold in 37 countries around the world, including the U.S., Australia, and countries in Europe.
  In recent years, environmental considerations have made it increasingly difficult to procure high-quality timber. In addition, creosote oil, which is used as a wood preservative, is expected to face restrictions on its use in the EU
due to carcinogenicity concerns. As a result, adoption of resin railway sleepers (FFU railway sleepers) as an alternative to wooden sleepers is accelerating.

 Business Strategies                 Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-potential Businesses: Pharmaceutical Sciences
With growing awareness of the importance of stable pharmaceutical supplies and increasingly sophisticated drug discovery, there has been rising demand in recent years for advanced contract services for R&D and manufacturing,
as well as high-value-added materials needed to develop pharmaceutical products.
   In the Pharmaceutical Sciences Business, we will establish a foundation for sustainable growth by building a system that consistently supports increasingly sophisticated pharmaceutical research, development, and
manufacturing through drug discovery support services (CRO) and contract manufacturing (CDMO) of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and intermediates. We will also enter the field of advanced medicine, using the supply
of scaffold materials that enable complex cell culture processes required in regenerative medicine and other fields as a foothold, with the aim of supporting the global advancement of medicine and a healthy, long-lived society.

Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 (FY2026-2028)

 Business Strategies                  Strategies for Enhancement Areas/Growth-potential Businesses: SEKISUI SOLAR FILM — Film-type Perovskite Solar Cells
Next-generation solar cells, which are said to be the key to realizing a decarbonized society, use semiconductors with a perovskite crystal structure as the material for power generation. Unlike conventional silicon solar cells, these
cells can be manufactured by applying the material to a film as if it were printed. They have the potential to spread to urban areas where installation sites are limited, and are expected to contribute to the spread of renewable
energy and the realization of carbon neutrality. The manufacturing process utilizes our proprietary technologies in sealing, process, materials, and film formation. For sealing resin, we have patented the optimal composition of our
proprietary material specifically designed for perovskite. To this point, we have conducted accelerated tests in accordance with standards for solar cell reliability, and confirmed durability equivalent to 10 years of outdoor exposure.
Film-type perovskite solar cells are ultra-lightweight and flexible, allowing them to be installed on the walls of buildings and other structures, as well as on roofs with weight constraints.
   On December 25, 2024, the project was selected for the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry’s GX Supply Chain Construction Support Project. The business commenced in March 2026, and concrete discussions began with
customers regarding supply.

Message from the New Head
of the Business Strategy Department                                                  Q          You were appointed Head of the Business Strategy Department in March 2026.

                                                                                      01        Looking back on your career to date, could you tell us about the principles you value
                                                                                                and what you keep in mind when making management decisions?
                                                                                     I have spent most of my career in the field of corporate management, working in taxation, corporate
                                                                                     planning, finance and accounting, and business strategy. Building a foundation for understanding
                                                                                     management through numbers early in my career has been an invaluable asset.
                                                                                         In my late twenties, I was seconded to a U.S. company shortly after it was acquired. With almost no
                                                                                     other Japanese employees in the workplace, I learned that nothing would move forward unless I clearly
                                                                                     articulated my own views. I believe that experience has shaped my approach to work ever since.
                                                                                         I spent the longest part of my career in corporate planning. Beginning in 1998, when the Company
                                                                                     posted losses for four consecutive years, I saw firsthand senior management being forced to make
                                                                                     difficult decisions. In 2000, while the Company was still in the red, we introduced the Divisional
                                                                                     Company System, which remains the basis of SEKISUI CHEMICAL’s organizational structure today.
                                                                                     While implementing emergency management measures, I experienced firsthand both the
                                                                                     importance and difficulty of simultaneously carrying out reforms with an eye to the future.
                                                                                         I then took charge of corporate management at the Urban Infrastructure & Environmental
                                                                                     Products Company in 2009. At the time, we also needed to restructure businesses following M&A. I
                                                                                     experienced the reorganization, transfer, and withdrawal of acquired businesses, which in some
                                                                                     respects proved even more difficult than the acquisitions themselves. This also trained me to make
                                                                                     decisions with a rigorous focus on future returns rather than the scale of investments already made.
                                                                                         For roughly the past decade, I have been responsible for finance and accounting at corporate
                                                                                     headquarters, and I now serve as Head of the Business Strategy Department. In communicating with
                                                                                     President Shimizu, I try to focus not simply on what options are available, but on what our first choice
                                                                                     is, and why, so that I can support his decision-making. Having spent much of my career in corporate
                                                                                     management, it is relatively easy for me to point out risks and apply the brakes. However, what the
                                                                                     Company needs most now is disciplined risk-taking based on a careful assessment of the risks so
                                                                                     that we do not miss opportunities. This is something I also make a conscious effort to keep in mind
                                                                                     when communicating with President Shimizu.

           How will you strengthen the management foundation that supports corporate value,
           including internal control and DX?

In internal control, we are shifting from post-incident response to proactive prevention across all five
areas of major incidents. Rather than simply detecting information leaks or accounting fraud after
they occur, we are focusing on putting systems and business processes in place to prevent incidents
from occurring in the first place. We also recognize that risks change as new businesses emerge and
market conditions evolve. Accordingly, each divisional company and business division regularly
provides opportunities to continuously reassess what constitutes a risk now and implement
appropriate countermeasures.
    In DX, we have worked to build a foundation that enables the use of standardized data across the
Company, including through the introduction of an integrated ERP (SAP) system. The next step is to
utilize that data to strengthen internal control and competitiveness. We are also using AI to improve
operational efficiency, but going forward, we will expand its use into areas directly linked to business

Medium-term Management Plan, Accelerate 2028 (FY2026-2028)

Foundation Strengthening            Innovation
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group emphasizes innovation as a key driver for continuously creating products to enhance sustainability in order to realize our Long-term Vision, Vision 2030.
  The source of innovation is the cycle of strategic foresight, processing, and value transformation, which is the business model of the value creation process.
  As we face a mountain of extremely difficult and pressing social issues, such as climate change, innovation to create new means of solving problems is becoming increasingly important.
  We will enhance our ability to solve social issues by quickly creating new value through the discovery of business opportunities across business domains, strengthening core technologies, and focusing on collaboration and open
innovation with external parties.

 Quality
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group strengthens basic quality while adhering strictly to quality compliance. By continuously working to strengthen the foundations that support quality, such as preventing defects from occurring and
reinforcing daily management, we are striving to create a corporate culture that places the highest priority on quality and prevents the occurrence of fraud. Based on the motto “We consider customer feedback as the beginning of
our manufacturing,” we are actively working on innovations in “quality of people,” “quality of systems,” and “quality of goods (products and services),” aiming to realize “quality that makes us the first choice.”

 Legal and Ethical
SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group established its Compliance Declaration in 2003, based on principles such as contributing to society, being a trusted company, and adhering to both the letter and spirit of the law. In accordance with
these principles, as well as the values set forth in the Group’s corporate philosophy and Code of Conduct, we have clearly expressed our commitment to earning the trust of society through compliance. We are working to further
strengthen compliance management by promoting a variety of programs.

   Corporate Governance

   Corporate Governance System
   Basic Policy
   SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group has put in place a basic philosophy regarding corporate governance that lays out efforts for securing sustainable growth and increasing corporate value over the medium to long term. To help achieve
   these goals, we are increasing the transparency and fairness of our management and pursuing swift decision-making and will do so while continuing to meet—through the creation of value for society that is part of our Corporate
   Philosophy—the needs of the five types of stakeholders the Group emphasizes: customers, shareholders, employees, business partners, and local communities and the environment.

  Risk Management
  In order to realize our long-term vision in a drastically changing business environment, it is essential for us to actively and decisively take risks and earn the trust, expectations, and sense of security of our
  stakeholders. We believe that risk control and resilience are the keys to achieving this, and we have positioned risk management as one of the foundations of our management.


  Risk Management System                                                                                                                                                                           Concept of Risk Management in SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group

  SEKISUI CHEMICAL Group takes an integrated approach to risk                                                                                                                    Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)                                                                                     Crisis management
